grammar.label: would and used to for past habit
grammar.form: would + base verb; used to + base verb
grammar.meaning: a repeated past action, or a past state that has ended

explanation.en: Both describe a past habit, but 'would' cannot carry a state: 'We used to live in Nukus' is right and 'We would live in Nukus' is not. 'Would' also needs a time frame already set, which is why it rarely opens a paragraph.
explanation.uz: Ikkalasi ham o'tmishdagi odatni bildiradi, lekin 'would' holatni ifodalay olmaydi: 'We used to live in Nukus' to'g'ri, 'We would live…' xato.

grammar.positive_example: Every summer my grandfather would walk to the market before dawn.
grammar.negative_example: My grandfather would own a small shop near the station.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida takroriy o'tmish bitta shakl bilan beriladi, shuning uchun holat va harakat farqi e'tibordan chetda qoladi.

grammar.label: state verbs in the continuous — a deliberate shift
grammar.form: be + verb-ing with a normally stative verb
grammar.meaning: turns a state into something temporary, changing or deliberate

explanation.en: State verbs normally resist the continuous, but breaking the rule carries meaning: 'I am thinking' (activity) against 'I think' (opinion); 'You are being difficult' (behaviour now) against 'You are difficult' (character). The continuous makes it temporary.
explanation.uz: Holat fe'llari odatda davomli shaklda kelmaydi, lekin qoidani ataylab buzish ma'no beradi: 'You are being difficult' — hozirgi xatti-harakat, 'You are difficult' — xarakter.

grammar.positive_example: You are being unusually careful today.
grammar.negative_example: I am knowing the answer already.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilida davomiylik alohida shakl bilan berilmaydi, shuning uchun holat fe'llarini davomli qilib qo'yish keng tarqalgan.

story.title: We used to do it differently

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: We used to leave at six. My father would walk the road first, in the dark, before the bus went.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Every winter morning. In summer he would sleep like anybody else.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Used to' for the years, 'would' for the mornings.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Used to' can hold a state. 'We used to have one bus.' 'Would' cannot.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: 'We would have one bus' means something else.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It means nothing at all, or something about a different year. That is the line between them.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Sarah said something odd yesterday. 'I am thinking the road is fine.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: She was being careful. 'I think' is the opinion. 'I am thinking' is the opinion with a door left open.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: So she may change her mind.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And she has told you so without saying it. That is what the continuous does to a state verb.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: My father never needed a tense for that. He just walked the road.
